text: The following propositional statement is (P ⇒ (Q ∨ R)) ⇒ ((P ∧ Q) ⇒ R)
solution: It is false when P=T, Q=T, R=F, so it cannot be valid. It is true when P=T, Q=T, R=T, so it is satisfiable. Simplifying, the formula reduces to ¬Q ∨ (¬P ∨ R), a contingency.

answer_evidence: Answer a It is false when P = T, Q = T, R = F and hence cannot be valid.
